items.stem: The clearest difference between engagement and satisfaction is that engagement reflects:

options.text: How content people are with pay and perks
options.rationale: That is closer to satisfaction with conditions.

options.text: People's commitment and willingness to give discretionary effort
options.rationale: Correct: engagement is about effort and commitment, not just contentment.

options.text: How many people attend social events
options.rationale: Attendance is not a measure of engagement.

options.text: Whether the office has good facilities
options.rationale: Facilities relate to conditions, not engagement.

items.explanation: Correct: engagement is about effort and commitment, not just contentment.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: The most common reason engagement surveys fail to improve anything is that:

options.rationale: Question length is rarely the core failure.

options.text: Results are collected but no visible action follows
options.rationale: Correct: inaction after surveys erodes trust and change.

options.text: Too few people are allowed to respond
options.rationale: Low response is a data issue, not the main failure of impact.

options.text: The survey is run too rarely to matter
options.rationale: Frequency helps, but acting on results matters more.

items.explanation: Correct: inaction after surveys erodes trust and change.

items.stem: Which TWO everyday manager behaviours most support engagement? (Select TWO)

options.text: Recognising good work specifically and promptly
options.rationale: Correct: timely, specific recognition reinforces effort.

options.text: Creating safety for people to raise concerns
options.rationale: Correct: psychological safety lets people contribute and flag issues.

options.text: Reserving all feedback for the annual review
Taking credit for the team's results
options.rationale: Claiming others' credit undermines trust and engagement.

items.explanation: Correct: timely, specific recognition reinforces effort.; Correct: psychological safety lets people contribute and flag issues.
